Signaling pathways related to the mechanism of action of DAMPs after TBI

Signaling pathways related to the mechanism of action of DAMPs after TBI. Following TBI, various nerve cells—including neurons, microglia, and astrocytes—endogenously release a range of DAMP proteins into the extracellular space. (a) These DAMPs can bind to specific receptors, such as membrane-bound TLRs. TLR2 and TLR4 are recognized by intracellular proteins (e.g. HMGB1, HSPs, and histones) as well as extracellular matrix components (e.g. LMW-HA). Free mtDNA, outside the cell, is delivered into the cell by endosomes through endocytosis, subsequently binding to TLR9 on the endosomal membrane. Upon activation by these DAMPs, TLRs initiate downstream signaling cascades via the adaptor protein MyD88. MyD88 then activates MAPKs and IKKs, leading to the production of inflammatory cytokines by nuclear transcription factors, such as AP-1 and NFκB; additionally, after HSP binds to CD40, it activates IKK, thereby inducing the NFκB inflammation-related pathway. (b) Exogenous HMGB1, S100B, and Aβ can drive pro-inflammatory responses by binding to the RAGE, subsequently initiating multiple signaling pathways, including the MAPK and JAK–STAT pathways. These pathways further influence various transcription factors, including NF-κB, AP-1, and STAT3, promoting the expression of pro-inflammatory genes and regulating cell migration, proliferation, and apoptosis; within the TREM family, TREM1 and TREM2 are key receptors activated by HMGB1 and HSP, which leads to further activation of the AKT–NF-κB pathway through PI3K or the NF-κB or AP-1 pathways via MAPK. LMW-HA activates the PI3K–AKT–NF-κB signaling pathway by binding to CD44, promoting neuroinflammation. (c) When nuclear DNA is damaged or exogenous DNA fragments are transported into cells via EVs, AIM2 is activated, initiating the assembly of AIM2 inflammasomes and inducing nonclassical pyroptosis pathways. Excessive tissue damage leads to the leakage of DNA fragments into the cytoplasm, including exogenous mtDNA that enters the cell via endocytosis and exogenous DNA that enters via EVs. These fragments can all activate the cGAS signaling pathway, promoting the production of the second messenger cGAMP that binds to the STING, located in the ER. STING then activates TBK1 and IKK on the Golgi apparatus, leading to the production of interferons and inflammatory cytokines through transcription factors IRF3 and NF-κB. (d) The NLRP3 inflammasome can be activated by various DAMPs, including CL from mitochondria, extracellular Aβ, and S100B, which is transported into cells via EVs, resulting in the secretion of IL-1β and IL-18 through GSDMD and inducing classic pyroptosis; the activation of P2X7R by extracellular ATP triggers the formation of nonselective pores, leading to calcium influx and potassium efflux, which may promote NLRP3 inflammasome activation; the color of the arrows corresponds to that of the molecule from which the arrow originates. TLRs toll-like receptors, HMGB1 high-mobility group box protein 1, HSPs heat shock proteins, LMW-HA low-molecular-weight hyaluronan, mtDNA mitochondrial DNA, MyD88 myeloid differentiation primary response 88, MAPKs mitogen-activated protein kinases, IKKs IκB kinases, AP-1 activator protein 1, NFκB nuclear factor κB, EVs extracellular vesicles, AIM2 absent in melanoma 2, CL cardiolipin, Aβ β-amyloid protein, GSDMD gasdermin D, cGAS cyclic guanosine monophosphate–adenylate synthase, STING stimulator of interferon genes, ER endoplasmic reticulum, TBK1 TANK-binding kinase 1, RAGE receptor of advanced glycation endproducts, NLRP3 NLR Family Pyrin Domain Containing 3
